answer: Marketplace-first execution is refuse-by-default until verify_package passes metadata, exact lockfile identity, private-only source, permission subset, freshness-bounded CRL, and HMAC-SHA256 over canonical bytes. Path coverage (AST) shows one sink caller (_after_choke) with choke lineno before sink lineno; a smuggle_unsigned mutant adds a second sink caller and the detector goes red. Unsigned-but-well-formed metadata is refused (signature-verification-failed) on every public path including execute_cached. A3 DESIGN.json is absent (ARC-0017); this unit specifies the choke without rebuilding the dossier. SUCCESS:ARC-0020

attack_classes.mapping: event-stream shipped a payload with more capability than consumers had reason to grant. verify_package refuses any permission not in the lockfile allowlist before the sink.
attack_classes.title: Malicious or over-permissioned package

attack_classes.mapping: crossenv existed because a near-name was installable. This client requires package.id == lockfile.packages[id].id and matching version; skill.helo is not skill.hello.
attack_classes.title: Typosquatted package id

attack_classes.mapping: Codecov customers ran an unsigned script whose bytes had changed. Metadata-valid packages with a missing or wrong hmac-sha256 MAC are refused at the signature step; execute_package_content is not called.
attack_classes.title: Unsigned or signature-stripped artifact

attack_classes.mapping: Birsan's installers consulted a public index when a private name collided. This client has no fetch_public path (AST-proven) and refuses allow_public_fallback=true and any source_registry other than the private index id.
attack_classes.title: Private-mirror vs public-index confusion

attack_classes.mapping: A yanked or patched Log4j release did not move clients whose lockfile/cache still held 2.14.1. execute_cached is a public execute path and still calls verify_package, which fail-closes on a stale CRL and on a revoked id.

prior_art.incident: Log4Shell CVE-2021-44228 — patched release vs pinned/cached install

attack_classes.title: Revocation that never reaches an already-installed client

claim_under_test: A marketplace client that validates package metadata may execute package content; signature, identity, source, permission, and revocation checks can be skipped for already-installed or lockfile-pinned packages.

claims.claim: Making the canonical registry index the control plane is sufficient to execute package content; no separate verify-before-execute choke is required.
claims.scoped_restatement: The index may be the control plane for what is listed. Execution still requires verify_package; without it, index-as-control-plane is a fail-open loader.
claims.why_locus: ARC-0017's architecture sentence makes the index the control plane and does not name a choke. That is a DESIGN gap in the A3 class, not a wording slip. This unit does not fill it by writing DESIGN.json.

claims.claim: A lockfile-pinned package is supply-chain safe, so already-installed content may run without re-verification.
claims.scoped_restatement: A lockfile pins id and version. Safety against signature-stripped or revoked-but-cached bytes requires the MAC and CRL steps on execute_cached as well as install.
claims.why_locus: lockfile-pinned is a catalogue phrase. DESIGN.json for A3 is absent, so there is no A3 rule to refute; the overclaim is the sentence that pinning implies byte safety.

claims.claim: Every public execute path in client.py reaches execute_package_content only after verify_package allows.
A package that passes metadata validation but fails signature verification is refused, including on execute_cached.
A2 marketplace_entry JSON is an executable A3 package and therefore a signature-stripped install path on this tree.
claims.scoped_restatement: A2 marketplace_entry is a generated metadata class with no signature field and no execute sink. It is not mapped as an A3 install path; treating it as one would be decorative.
claims.why_locus: ARC-0010 registry.schema.json marketplace_entry has no signature field and no execute sink. Calling that listing an A3 execute path is a sentence-level category error, not a reason to rebuild A2 DESIGN.json here.

cross_vendor_reviewer.reason: Catalog requires a Codex cross-vendor reviewer. Codex MCP is not available on this Linux substrate. Absence is recorded as NOT-CHECKED rather than a forged PASS.

dropped_threats.title: Marketplace moderation queue and publisher dispute process
dropped_threats.why_no_design_path: This client has no second publisher and no moderation object. Listing a dispute process would be decorative under PR-ONLY.

dropped_threats.title: Per-publisher public-key signatures and web-of-trust
dropped_threats.why_no_design_path: No second publisher keyring exists in the client. HMAC with the owner key is the implemented binding; a PKI gate with no keys would be an unfalsifiable control.

dropped_threats.title: SBOM CVE scanner as a blocking install gate
dropped_threats.why_no_design_path: No scanner binary or advisory feed is invoked from client.py. Claiming CVE blocking without a call site would be overclaim.

question: Threat-model the marketplace as an attack surface: malicious or over-permissioned package, typosquatted id, unsigned or signature-stripped artifact, dependency confusion between a private mirror and a public one, and a revocation that never reaches an already-installed client. Specify the MANDATORY verification a client performs before executing ANY package content, and prove no install path skips it.

reviewer.method: Mechanical scope check: REFUTED rows name DESIGN vs SENTENCE; attack classes cite dated URLs mapped onto resolving design paths; dropping defect_locus fails the checker; unsigned metadata-valid packages are refused. Agreement with the A3 class is not required.

scenario.catching_architecture: A3 marketplace-first with mandatory verify_package before execute_package_content on every public lifecycle path in command-center/p2-wave/probes/ARC-0020/client.py, including execute_cached.
procedure: Build a lockfile pinning skill.hello@1.0.0 from owner-private-index.
Build a package with valid id/version/source/permissions and an HMAC over those bytes.
Strip or zero the signature field while leaving metadata intact.
Offer the stripped package to every PUBLIC_EXECUTE_PATHS entry, including execute_cached.
Assert each path returns executed=False with reason signature-verification-failed.
scenario.title: Metadata-valid signature-stripped package must not execute

strongest_surviving_counterargument: Under PR-ONLY the owner is the only publisher, so HMAC-SHA256 with the owner key is the smallest binding that still fails closed on stripped bytes. A second publisher would make this MAC insufficient (no per-publisher keys). That is dead-weight under the single-owner cost model, not a reason to skip the choke. The index can remain the control plane for what is listed; it is not a substitute for verify-before-execute. Do not rebuild A3 DESIGN.json in this unit (no ADV circle). Generated A2 marketplace_entry JSON is metadata-only and is not an execute path.
title: A3 (marketplace-first): Marketplace threat model and mandatory verify-before-execute choke

upstream_design.note: ARC-0017 is not delivered on this worktree. This unit specifies the mandatory verification choke and maps threats onto that choke. It does not write command-center/phase3/A3/DESIGN.json.
